Article (plain text of the PDF):

Preprint
Biological Physics

Eleven exactly certified violations of the proofreading
bound e−2∆ among 88 two-bound-state networks
Colin Ji, Laurenz Thümmler, Noah Schittenhelm and Ali Suleman
ETH Zürich, Switzerland
Preprint, October 2026

Abstract We ask whether the Hopfield error bound of
kinetic proofreading holds universally for Markov networks with two bound states and fuel-driven steps. For
the linear Hopfield chain with n = 2, η ≥ e−3∆ is proved
for all positive rates and fuel potentials by a symbolic
coefficient-positivity argument. The enumerated family
has 88 admissible members. For 50 of them, η ≥ e−2∆ is
proved symbolically; 11 have exact rational-arithmetic
certificates of violation, with η down to 1.386398e-12;
27 remain open. Hence e−2∆ is violated by 11 of these
networks. The classification is computer-assisted: the
bounds are symbolic, and the violations are exact rational certificates at specific rates. Whether the 27 open
members obey the bound, and which structural feature
causes violations, remains open.

A violation must be exact, which excludes rounding
artefacts. We therefore pair symbolic positivity proofs
for bounds with exact rational certificates for violations.
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows that the family with two bound
states has 88 admissible members, of which 50 obey
η ≥ e−2∆ , 11 have certified violations and 27 are
open.
• Theorem 2 shows an exactly certified violation for
fam2_66, with η = 5.082802e-07.
• Theorem 3 shows two further exact violations,
fam2_9 and fam2_11.
• Theorem 4 shows exact violations for 10 topologies
jointly, which adds eight to those of Theorem 3.
• The Hopfield-chain theorem shows that η ≥ e−3∆
holds for the chain with n = 2 for all positive rates
and fuel potentials.
• The 50-topology theorem shows that η ≥ 1/D2 is
proved symbolically for 50 topologies of the family,
where 1/D2 is the bound e−2∆ of the classification.

Keywords kinetic proofreading · Hopfield bound · error
rate · exact certificates · Markov networks · entropy
production

1 Introduction
Kinetic proofreading increases specificity beyond what
free-energy differences or kinetic barriers alone allow, if
the reaction is strongly but nonspecifically driven [1].
The ultimate accuracy of error-correcting pathways is set
by the displacement from equilibrium of the driving nucleoside triphosphates [2]. Several checking steps reach a
given accuracy at lower dissipation than a single step [2].
Pareto fronts for energy-relay proofreading yield tradeoff relations and scaling laws [3], and a dynamical phase
transition has been reported in the mixed regime [3]. In
the generalized Hopfield model, more proofreading steps
give better trade-offs [4], and the scaling relations were
studied numerically [4]. A kinetically controlled bound
on error for proofreading networks has been derived [5],
and experimental systems have been compared with it
[5]. Asymptotic scaling analyses of arbitrary networks,
inspired by Hopfield’s treatment, have also been given
[6].
The open question is whether the Hopfield bound η ≥
e−(n+1)∆ is a universal limit for all networks with a fixed
number of bound states, or whether topologies with fueldriven discard pathways break it. The question is hard
because the topology space is combinatorial and the rate
space is high-dimensional, and numerical optima cannot
establish a bound. A lower bound must hold for all rates.

2 Setting
All parameters are fixed by the model. The discrimination free-energy difference is ∆ = ln 100, so e∆ = 100
and e−∆ = 0.01. The wrong substrate W leaves bound
states e∆ times faster than the right substrate R. Both
substrates traverse the same Markov network, every
edge has a reverse edge, and local detailed balance holds.
Cycle affinities arise only from the fuel potential µ ≥ 0
per fuel-driven activation and µP ≥ 0 per product, both
explored in [0, 20]. Concentrations are absorbed into
the binding rates. All rates, including derived reverse
rates, lie in [e−L , eL ] with L = 10. A network has at
most 10 states (unbound states plus R and W copies
of bound states). Rates are rounded to rationals with
denominator at most 106 for exact certificates. The
enumerated family has k = 2 bound states.
Observables are the error rate η = JW /JR , the dissipation σ (entropy production per product, in kT ), and
the speed v = JR . We write D = e∆ and G = eµ . The
bound 1/D2 of the proved family is the bound e−2∆ of
the classification.
Four are degenerate (no net production possible, η =
0/0) and are excluded, leaving 88. Two certificate types
are used:
